problem: Existing map-based VLN agents ignore perceptual uncertainty (unreliable grounding among look-alike structures, occlusion-induced traversability ambiguity) and predict actions regardless of confidence.
motivation: Uncertainty signals the reliability of perception and feasibility of actions. Explicit 3D Gaussian primitives give physically meaningful per-primitive attributes, so uncertainty can be estimated locally and fed to the policy.
key_idea: Build a Semantic Gaussian Map from panoramic RGB-D, estimate per-Gaussian geometric (variational), semantic (variational) and appearance (Fisher Information) uncertainty, and attach them to the Gaussians as a 3D Value Map that feeds a DUET-style action predictor.
insight: Both the SGM and the uncertainty contribute, and they are complementary: on R2R SR, the DUET baseline scores 72.22, SGM alone 76.21, uncertainty alone 74.20 and the full model 78.32. Geometric+semantic uncertainty helps more than appearance alone, and all three together are best. Scaling uncertainty to 0 in 10 complex scenes drops success from 10/10 to 2/10, while simple scenes are unaffected. Adding a rendered 2D uncertainty map to DUET, BEVBert and VER gives more than 1 SR point each, so the cue is transferable. Moderate Gaussian pruning gives a speedup, while aggressive pruning hurts.
method: Semantic Gaussian Map: back-project RGB-D into a pseudo-lidar cloud to initialize 3D Gaussians; attach SAM2-segment CLIP embeddings as semantic attributes; optimize with RGB (L1+SSIM), depth and semantic rendering losses; prune Gaussians with small scale (tau_e) or low opacity (tau_alpha).
Geometric uncertainty: learn variational perturbations of Gaussian position and scale (ELBO, Gaussian and uniform priors); U^g is the summed L2 norm of the posterior standard deviations.
Semantic uncertainty: same variational scheme on the semantic attribute with geometry fixed; U^s is the L2 norm of the posterior std.

Appearance uncertainty: Fisher Information (outer product of rendering gradients) approximating the Hessian of the reconstruction loss, block-diagonal per Gaussian; U^a is the log-determinant of the block.

3D Value Map: each Gaussian is a 20-d vector (geometry, color, semantics, 3 uncertainties). It is projected to 768-d, aggregated, concatenated with the instruction embedding and passed through a transformer to get candidate-node scores, mapped to actions by nearest neighbour. It is an extra branch on DUET's 2D pathway and topological memory.
Training: DUET-style pretraining (MLM, SAP, OG for REVERIE; 100k iterations) then DAgger finetuning (25k iterations).

setting.backbone: DUET-style dual-scale topological transformer with an added 3D Value Map branch; SAM2 + CLIP for semantic attributes
setting.training_data: R2R / RxR / REVERIE training sets only (MLM, SAP, OG pretraining then DAgger finetuning); no extra data reported
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph candidate viewpoints in a topological map, plus STOP

numbers_note: The main tables print R2R SR/SPL as integers. Ablation tables give R2R val-unseen SR 78.32 / SPL 66.47 and REVERIE SR 53.37, which differs from the 56.37 in the main REVERIE table; this inconsistency is in the paper.
results: The method reaches R2R val-unseen SR 78 / SPL 66 versus 3DGS-VLN 77/66 and VER 76/65. On RxR val-unseen it gets SR 65.2 / nDTW 65.6 versus BEVBert 64.1 / 63.9. On REVERIE val-unseen it gets RGS 37.65 / RGSPL 27.01 versus 3DGS-VLN 36.73 / 26.74. It adds about 1.35 s per step over DUET.
limitations: Evaluated only in the static Matterport3D simulator on indoor tasks, with no real-robot or dynamic-scene tests.
Uncertainty is estimated passively from the current views without active perception, and it adds latency (SAM2 costs 1.47 s); failure cases include premature stopping.
Gains over the strongest baselines are small (1-2 points), and some numbers are inconsistent between tables.
